automatic tank water filling system and the automatic watering system. Most
importantly, this system is flexible and customizable to users. The system allows the

2.1 Related Theory
2.1.1 Fertilizer [3]
A fertilizer (American English) or fertiliser (British English) is any material of
natural or synthetic origin that is applied to soil or to plant tissues to supply plant
nutrients. Fertilizers may be distinct from liming materials or other non-nutrient soil
amendments. Many sources of fertilizer exist, both natural and industrially produced.
For most modern agricultural practices, fertilization focuses on three main macro
nutrients: Nitrogen (N), Phosphorus (P), and Potassium (K) with occasional addition of
supplements like rock dust for micronutrients. Farmers apply these fertilizers in a
variety of ways: through dry or pelletized or liquid application processes, using large
agricultural equipment or hand-tool methods.

Mechanism of Fertilizer
Six tomato plants grown with and without nitrate fertilizer on nutrient-poor
sand/clay soil. One of the plants in the nutrient-poor soil has died. Fertilizers enhance
the growth of plants. This goal is met in two ways, the traditional one being additives
that provide nutrients. The second mode by which some fertilizers act is to enhance the
effectiveness of the soil by modifying its water retention and aeration. This article, like
many on fertilizers, emphasizes the nutritional aspect. Fertilizers typically provide, in
varying proportions:
Three main macronutrients:
- Nitrogen (N): leaf growth.
- Phosphorus (P): Development of roots, flowers, seeds, fruit.
- Potassium (K): Strong stem growth, movement of water in plants,
promotion of flowering and fruiting.

Three secondary macronutrients: calcium (Ca), magnesium (Mg), and sulfur(S);
Micronutrients: copper (Cu), iron (Fe), manganese (Mn), molybdenum (Mo),
zinc (Zn), boron (B). Of occasional significance are silicon (Si), cobalt (Co),
and vanadium (V).
NPK fertilizers
NPK fertilizers are three-component fertilizers providing nitrogen, phosphorus,
and potassium. There exist two types of NPK fertilizers: compound and blends.
Compound NPK fertilizers contain chemically bound ingredients, while blended NPK
fertilizers are physical mixtures of single nutrient components.
NPK rating is a rating system describing the amount of nitrogen, phosphorus,
and potassium in a fertilizer. NPK ratings consist of three numbers separated by dashes
(e.g., 10-10-10 or 16-4-8) describing the chemical content of fertilizers. The first
number represents the percentage of nitrogen in the product; the second number, P2O5;
the third, K2O. Fertilizers do not actually contain P2O5 or K2O, but the system is a
conventional shorthand for the amount of the phosphorus (P) or potassium (K) in a
fertilizer. A 50-pound (23 kg) bag of fertilizer labeled 16-4-8 contains 8 lb (3.6 kg) of
nitrogen (16% of the 50 pounds), an amount of phosphorus equivalent to that in 2
pounds of P2O5 (4% of 50 pounds), and 4 pounds of K2O (8% of 50 pounds). Most
fertilizers are labeled according to this N-P-K convention, although Australian
convention, following an N-P-K-S system, adds a fourth number for sulfur, and uses
elemental values for all values including P and K.
2.1.2 pH [4]
In chemistry, pH is a scale used to specify the acidity or basicity of an aqueous
solution. Acidic solutions (solutions with higher concentrations of H+ ions) are
measured to have lower pH values than basic or alkaline solutions.
Figure 2.2 Test tubes containing solutions of pH 1–10 colored with an indicator

The pH scale is logarithmic and inversely indicates the concentration of
hydrogen ions in the solution. This is because the formula used to calculate pH
approximates the negative of the base 10 logarithm of the molar concentration[a] of
hydrogen ions in the solution. More precisely, pH is the negative of the base 10
logarithm of the activity of the H+ ion.
At 25 °C, solutions with a pH less than 7 are acidic, and solutions with a pH
greater than 7 are basic. Solutions with a pH of 7 at this temperature are neutral (e.g.
pure water). The neutral value of the pH depends on the temperature, being lower than
7 if the temperature increases. The pH value can be less than 0 for very strong acids, or
greater than 14 for very strong bases.
The pH scale is traceable to a set of standard solutions whose pH is established
by international agreement. Primary pH standard values are determined using a
concentration cell with transference, by measuring the potential difference between a
hydrogen electrode and a standard electrode such as the silver chloride electrode. The
pH of aqueous solutions can be measured with a glass electrode and a pH meter, or a
color-changing indicator. Measurements of pH are important in chemistry, agronomy,
medicine, water treatment, and many other applications.

CONCLUSION AND DISCUSSION
5.1 Conclusion
The Intelligent watering system achieved the objective goal and gives an
impressive result. The system can perform well mixing fertilizer ingredients
accurately. The sensor work with no problems and the system is performing as
expected. The safety also exists to prevent unexpected process that might occur
during operation such as short circuit or motor overloading. The safety also prevents
the system form breaking down.
During developing the system, we faced with power problem and noise from
electronics components. But after fixing the power supply and adding electronic noise
cancelling part such as snubber circuit, surge suppressor, diode, and opto-isolated
relay the system can perform in a long period of time without any problems.
The system helps reduce a good amount of time from watering and fertilizing
plants and waste the comes from human error. The system performs accurately and
can be used in greenhouses, but the system needs to be checked and repair be for use
to get the best performance from it.

60
5.2 Discussion
The intelligent watering system has a lot of functions to cover all need for
plants, But the watering system is still cannot be used for plants that were planted in
soil. This system only supports hydro-phonic type of planting because the system
does not measure the moisture in the plot instead it measures the level of water in the
plot. However, to have the system be supported for soil planting, the system will have
to be designed and developed purposely for it.
In the system, there is still no button or faction to control the motors and
solenoid directly or manually. This function can allow users to use the system even
when the MCU is not working properly. This can be added in the future but is just not
added to the system yet.
This system cannot be further more than two meters from the sensors because
the signal can be lost in the wire. That can cause calculating analog signal to digital
inaccurate before sending the signal to the control unit such as Modbus or 4-20mA.
pH sensor and EC sensor that is used in this system is still not stable. The
sensor gives unstable output when the water is not still or when there is a lot amount
of water in the tank. This leads to problem of finding the exact number which will
have to be dealt with in the future.
This system is designed to be used in the location or area that accessing WIFI
is not possible. That means controlling the system remotely is not possible. To
develop the system to be controlled remotely, the system needs the module that can
access internet or micro controller that can be connected to internet to connect via
serial communication with Arduino mega 2560 that drives the system. Also, Lora-
wan technology will likely be the answer for this system.

EEPROM
The microcontroller on the Arduino AVR based board has EEPROM: memory
whose values are kept when the board is turned off (like a tiny hard drive). This
library enables you to read and write those bytes but it have a limited number of
writing (about 100,000 times)
The supported micro-controllers on the various Arduino boards have different
amounts of EEPROM: 1024 bytes on the ATmega328P, 512 bytes on the ATmega168
and ATmega8, 4 KB (4096 bytes) on the ATmega1280 and ATmega2560. The
Arduino boards have an emulated EEPROM space of 1024 bytes.
To use this library
#include <EEPROM.h>
Examples
EEPROM.Clear: Clear the bytes in the EEPROM.
EEPROM.Read: Read the EEPROM and send its values to the computer.
EEPROM.Write: Stores values from an analog input to the EEPROM.
EEPROM.Crc: Calculates the CRC of EEPROM contents as if it was an array.
EEPROM.Get: Get values from EEPROM and prints as float on serial.
EEPROM.Iteration: Understand how to go through the EEPROM memory locations.
EEPROM.Put: Put values in EEPROM using variable semantics.
EEPROM.Update: Stores values read from A0 into EEPROM, writing the value only
if different, to increase EEPROM life.

APPENDIX B
SNUBBER CIRCUIT
These circuits are very useful in handling the spikes of voltage that arise from
the operation of inductive loads. And we use it many point in the systems.
RC snubbers
A simple RC snubber uses a small resistor (R) in series with a small capacitor
(C) This combination can be used to suppress the rapid rise in voltage across a
thyristor, preventing the erroneous turn-on of the thyristor; it does this by limiting the
rate of rise in voltage (dV/dt) across the thyristor to a value which will not trigger it.
An appropriately-designed RC snubber can be used with either DC or AC loads. This
sort of snubber is commonly used with inductive loads such as electric motors. The
voltage across a capacitor cannot change instantaneously, so a decreasing transient
current will flow through it for a small fraction of a second, allowing the voltage
across the switch to increase more slowly when the switch is opened. Determination
of voltage rating can be difficult owing to the nature of transient waveforms, and may
be defined simply by the power rating of the snubber components and the application.
RC snubbers can be made discretely and are also built as a single component.
Diode snubbers
Main article: Flyback diode
When the current flowing is DC, a simple rectifier diode is often employed as
a snubber. The snubber diode is wired in parallel with an inductive load (such as a
relay coil or electric motor). The diode is installed so that it does not conduct under
normal conditions. When the external driving current is interrupted, the inductor
current flows instead through the diode. The stored energy of the inductor is then
gradually dissipated by the diode voltage drop and the resistance of the inductor itself.
One disadvantage of using a simple rectifier diode as a snubber is that the diode
allows current to continue flowing for some time, causing the inductor to remain
active for slightly longer than desired. When such a snubber is utilized in a relay, this
effect may cause a significant delay in the drop out, or disengagement, of the actuator.
The diode must immediately enter into forward conduction mode as the driving
current is interrupted. Most ordinary diodes, even "slow" power silicon diodes, are
able to turn on very quickly, in contrast to their slow reverse recovery time. These are
sufficient for snubbing electromechanical devices such as relays and motors.
In high-speed cases, where the switching is faster than 10 nanoseconds, such as in
certain switching power regulators, "fast", "ultrafast", or Schottky diodes may be
required.

2.1 Related Theory
Clustering algorithm is the unsupervised learning that deals with data structure
partition in unknown areas [2]. The complete definition for clustering described as instances
in the same cluster must be similar as much as possible and instances in the different clusters
must be different as much as possible. The traditional clustering algorithms can be divided
into 9 categories: Based on the partition, Based on the hierarchy, Based on fuzzy theory,
Based on distribution, Based on density, Based on graph theory, Based on the grid, Based on
fractal Theory, and Based on the model.
Silhouette coefficient is an evaluation indicator of clustering algorithms [3]. Which
evaluates the cluster based on the measure of the average distance between one data point and
other data points in the same clusters and the average distance among different clusters. The
silhouette value can vary between -1 and 1, with higher values indicating better-defined
clusters and lower values indicating poorly defined clusters.

2.3.1 Machine learning
- K-Means
K-Means is one of the simplest unsupervised learning algorithms based on
partitions that solve the well known clustering problem . The main idea is to define k
centroids, one for each cluster and take each point belonging to a given data set and
associate it to the nearest centroid. Then re-calculate k new centroids as centers of the
clusters resulting from the previous step. After these k new centroids, a new binding
has to be done between the same data points and the nearest new centroid. A loop has
been generated. As a result of this loop it may notice that the k centroids change their
location step by step until no more changes are done.
- Agglomerative hierarchical clustering
Agglomerative hierarchical clustering is hierarchy-based clustering since it
builds a binary merge tree starting from leaves that contain data elements to the
root that contains the full data-set. The graphical representation of that tree that
embeds the nodes on the plane is called a dendrogram. To implement a hierarchical
clustering algorithm, one has to choose a linkage function that defines the distance
between any two subsets . A hierarchical clustering is monotonous if and only if the
similarity decreases along the path from any leaf to the root, otherwise there exists at
least one inversion.

CHAPTER 5
CONCLUSION AND DISCUSSION
5.1 Conclusion
The objective of this project was to create a website utilizing machine learning-based
clustering to comprehend the characteristics and preferred travel behavior of a sample of Thai
people for domestic tourism post the COVID-19 pandemic. The goal is to suggest tour
packages that align with user preferences. In the machine learning component, Principal
Component Analysis (PCA) was applied to reduce the data's dimensionality, and K-means
clustering was employed as the grouping algorithm. The optimal model configuration
involved K-means clustering with PCA on 527 samples. Clustering the samples into three
groups resulted in an optimal silhouette score of 0.405. The characteristics derived from this
clustering will be leveraged to enhance the tourism industry by recommending tour packages
for domestic travel.
5.2 Discussion
Due to the evaluation metric, we have chosen a k-cluster value of 3. However, the
optimal k obtained from the elbow method is 4. The reason for selecting 3 clusters is based
on a comparison with the silhouette coefficient score. Specifically, the silhouette score for 3
clusters is approximately 0.405, while the elbow method indicates a value of around 800. On
the other hand, if we were to use 4 clusters, the silhouette score would decrease to 0.36, and
the elbow method suggests a value of around 600. Comparing the transition from 2 clusters to
3 clusters, the elbow method decreases from 1400 to 800. Consequently, we have decided to
proceed with 3 clusters.
Key successes of the project include the seamless integration of the machine learning
model with the web application and the intuitive UX/UI design that enhances user interaction.
Challenges such as ensuring responsive design and integrating complex datasets were
effectively addressed. The use of modern web technologies and frameworks has allowed for
scalable and maintainable web architecture. Future enhancements could include expanding
the recommendation engine's capabilities and incorporating real-time data for more dynamic
travel suggestions. The project's impact lies in its innovative approach to personalized travel
planning, setting a new standard for travel websites.
Another possibility is to enhance clustering performance to ensure higher accuracy in
matching the right touring package to a customer.

University provides another way for students and employees to get access. It changes
from card exchange to vehicle registration. People that already registered the car have
to stick the sticker that shows the vehicle number in front of the car. People who have
registered this access card will be able to enter and exit the university without having
to exchange any card. This way reduces traffic congestion while card exchange. But
this sticker cannot provide the time of entry and exit of each vehicle, making it still
lacking safety. In addition, the sticker must be registered at the building division. Some
people may be inconvenienced to submit documents and therefore still use the card
exchange to enter and exit university. As a result, the problem remains the same.

management system. This system will make people easy to enter to university by
register the car to the system and then getting the access card for the car. The access
card made from RFID technology. People have scan access cards with RFID readers
and the system will send data to the server. The system will collect the data and can

2.3.1 RFID radio-frequency identification
RFID is an acronym for “radio-frequency identification” and refers to a
technology whereby digital data encoded in RFID tags or smart labels (defined below)
are captured by a reader via radio waves. RFID is similar to barcoding in that data from
a tag or label are captured by a device that stores the data in a database. RFID, however,
has several advantages over systems that use barcode asset tracking software. The most

14
notable is that RFID tag data can be read outside the line-of-sight, whereas barcodes
must be aligned with an optical scanner. If you are considering implementing an RFID
solution, take the next step and contact the RFID experts at AB&R® (American
Barcode and RFID).
Figure 2.1 RFID
RFID belongs to a group of technologies referred to as Automatic
Identification and Data Capture (AIDC). AIDC methods automatically identify objects,
collect data about them, and enter those data directly into computer systems with little
or no human intervention. RFID methods utilize radio waves to accomplish this. At a
simple level, RFID systems consist of three components: an RFID tag or smart label,
an RFID reader, and an antenna. RFID tags contain an integrated circuit and an antenna,
which are used to transmit data to the RFID reader (also called an interrogator). The
reader then converts the radio waves to a more usable form of data. Information
collected from the tags is then transferred through a communications interface to a host
computer system, where the data can be stored in a database and analyzed at a later
time.
As stated above, an RFID tag consists of an integrated circuit and an antenna.
The tag is also composed of a protective material that holds the pieces together and
shields them from various environmental conditions. The protective material depends
on the application. For example, employee ID badges containing RFID tags are
typically made from durable plastic, and the tag is embedded between the layers of
plastic. RFID tags come in a variety of shapes and sizes and are either passive or active.
Passive tags are the most widely used, as they are smaller and less expensive to
implement. Passive tags must be “powered up” by the RFID reader before they can
transmit data. Unlike passive tags, active RFID tags have an onboard power supply
(e.g., a battery), thereby enabling them to transmit data at all times. For a more detailed
discussion, refer to this article: Passive RFID Tags vs. Active RFID Tags.
Smart labels differ from RFID tags in that they incorporate both RFID and
barcode technologies. They’re made of an adhesive label embedded with an RFID tag
inlay, and they may also feature a barcode and/or other printed information. Smart
labels can be encoded and printed on-demand using desktop label printers, whereas
programming RFID tags are more time consuming and requires more advanced
equipment.

3.1 Workflow
We have simulated how our system works as a workflow in Figure 3.1.
In the system's operational process, users are required to perform a login before
accessing its functionalities. If a user is not logged into the system, they will not have the
privilege to use its features. The login process is divided into two categories: first, logging in
as a regular user, and second, logging in as an administrator. Upon successful login, users will
be directed to the main homepage as the default landing page. This differs for administrators,
who will have access to a user management menu. Regular users will not see this menu
appear in their navigation bar.
Following the homepage, there will be a product management menu where users can
choose to either sell products or add products to the inventory. If a user opts to add products,
the system will check whether the user has already created that particular product. If not, the
user will need to create the product first. Once the product is successfully created, the user
can then add it to the system. In the final step, after the user successfully adds a product, the
system will update the inventory stock to reflect the addition of the new product. This ensures
that the stock levels are accurately maintained in the system, accounting for any changes
made through the addition of products. In the sales process, when a user intends to sell a
product, the system will verify whether the desired quantity of the product is available in the
inventory. If the quantity is insufficient, the user will need to add more of that product to the
inventory. If the product quantity is adequate, the user can proceed with the sale, and the
system will deduct the sold quantity from the inventory. This ensures that users can only sell
products that are currently in stock.

Hospital, with respect to the process of discharge planning. It allows a number of users
with different roles to input patient details and assessments, prior and after the discharge
from the in-hospital care. These include medical staffs working specific wards,
nutritionists, physical therapists, for instance. Previous assessment results can be
viewed as references for any new evaluation attempt. This is possible even after patients
having been transferred back to home care or local hospitals. As a result, the system
administrator is provided with details covering the actual in- and post-hospital recovery,
which can be obtained through reports. The proposed web application makes this entire
process transparent and efficient for all the parties, especially information after
discharging from the hospital that has been missing from the current working
procedure. In fact, this is highly useful as a means to justify the quality of medical
treatment as a whole.

“Seamless” discharge planning happens when a patient is effectively and safely

recover and avoid potentially avoidable readmissions. When it doesn’t, patients
boomerang for reasons such as falls, adverse drug events, worsening conditions, or new
conditions that could have been avoided if the patient stayed on the road to recovery.

3.5 Function design
UI – 01
How to use the login page (UI-01), fill in the username and password in the text
boxes, when complete the system will check the information that it matches the
information contained in the system or not. If the information matches in the system, it
will proceed to the next page. (data-page (UI-02)), but if the information is not correct,
there will be a notification that the information is incorrect and will be re-entered.
Figure 3.5 Function design UI-01

25
UI – 02
When entering this page It is divided into 2 functions: add new patient
information and select patient assessment. In the Add New Patient Information page, it
is the duty for the nurse to add the information of the patient to be assessed. When
the data is added and clicked successfully, the information will be saved and in the other
part, choosing to assess the patient will be a multidisciplinary function by pressing the
patient selection button to access the assessment page of each multidisciplinary.
Figure 3.6 Function design UI-02

26
UI – 03
On this page, when the Add button is pressed, the patient information will be
taken on this page and fill in the initial patient's information as a new patient. When
completed and click on the submit button, the new information that has just been added
will go into the database for further use. But if not submitting, the information will not
be added yet.
Figure 3.7 Function design UI-03

27
UI – 04
Operation procedures when pressing the Select button has 5 functions.
• View information: when clicking to view information, will go to the patient
information page for use in assessing.
• Evaluation: when pressed, will go to the patient assessment page according to
the page of their branch.
• Evaluation results: when pressed, the system will show the evaluation report
page.
• Discharge: when pressed, the system will discharge and change the patient's
status.
• After discharge: it will be a function for community hospitals to perform
retrospective assessment
Figure 3.8 Function design UI-04

28
UI – 05
When the selected patient and the AN to be assessed successfully. It will enter
a form that will be evaluated for each multidisciplinary. Multidisciplinary branch: Enter
the form and fill in the information on the multidisciplinary form page and submit the
information to the database (UI-06).
Figure 3.9 Function design UI-05

UI – 06
There are two parts to the evaluation process:
1 . Multidisciplinary assessment in which they are responsible the assessments
can be recorded multiple times and the name of the author will be recorded.
2. Assessors can view the most recent assessments of other branches, but not
edit them from the assessments of others.

CONCLUSION AND DISCUSSION
5.1 Conclusion
This project is a system that helps Chiang Rai Prachanukroh Hospital to collect
patient information more easily. By collecting our data we keep patient information
more organized and reduce the waste of patient information and the Hospital can
quickly access patient information and also be able to view information from various
departments but this application is for data input and reports, but still does not support
progress monitoring.
5.2 Discussion
Success
- A database system that can record and store patient information.
- The system is easy to use and help facilitate information storage for
hospital staff.
- It is convenient to record and search information.
- Keep patient information more organized and reduce data loss.
- Users can quickly access patient information from many departments.
Unsuccess
- The system can be accessed by a person who has been authorized.
- Able to use statistical data to analyze to improve the medical plan.(next
phase.)

2.1.1 DNA Space
Cisco DNA Spaces is a location-based services platform developed by
Cisco that uses Wi-Fi and other location technologies to provide real-time insights
and analytics for businesses and organizations.
Cisco DNA Spaces is designed to help organizations understand how
people move and behave within physical spaces such as buildings, campuses, and
stores. The platform can collect data from various sources, including Wi-Fi access
points, Bluetooth beacons, and other location sensors, and use this data to generate
insights and analytics that can help organizations optimize their operations,
improve customer experiences, and increase revenue.
2.1.2 Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE)
Also known as Bluetooth Smart, is a wireless technology designed for
low-power, low-latency communication between devices. BLE is a variant of the
Bluetooth wireless technology, and it was introduced in Bluetooth 4.0.
BLE is designed to enable wireless communication between small
devices with low power consumption requirements, such as sensors, wearables,
and other IoT devices. BLE is well-suited for these types of devices because it
uses significantly less power than traditional Bluetooth technology, which can
help to extend battery life.
One of the key features of BLE is its ability to operate in two different
modes: peripheral and central. In peripheral mode, the BLE device broadcasts its
presence and data to other devices in the vicinity, while in central mode, the BLE
device connects to and receives data from peripheral devices.
BLE also includes a number of security features to protect against
unauthorized access and data theft. These features include encryption and
authentication protocols, as well as the ability to set access control policies and
manage device permissions.

tablets, and other computing devices. This makes it a popular choice for

Beacons are transferred via the Bluetooth Low Energy standard –
BLE for short – already mentioned. With this radio technology, multiple devices
can be connected together. The advantage of BLE over other radio technologies
is that BLE can provide low power consumption and low cost. That is why BLE
is primarily used for mobile devices such as smartphones or smart watches. iOS
supports this standard from iOS7, Android from version 4.3 and Windows Phone
from Windows Phone 8. However, there is currently a problem with Android
devices: not all Android devices with at least Android version 4.3 installed can
communicate with beacons. It is possible that the Android device's hardware has
BLE capability, but the function is still not used due to the lack of ROM updates.
Beacons can be connected to devices, tools, and objects as Bluetooth beacons,
